artboards.title: The heading map — the whole feature

annotations.text:
CARDS = THE SPEC READ BACK AS THE THINKING BEHIND IT

Each section is a beat on one line of reasoning. Fixed labels, no Claude run: a heading looks up its role in the argument (THE PROBLEM, WHAT MUST BE TRUE, WHAT WE STILL DON'T KNOW) and the connective that leads into it — so who wants this? / which, to be buildable, means / and, just as deliberately / except that.

Under each title is a COUNTED line, not a written one: "7 criteria · 5 tied to a story · 2 need a look". Everything in it comes from parsing the markdown, so it is free and it can never drift from the document.

Beat 5 is the fallback: "## Rollout notes" is not in the map, so it arrives with a dashed node, a neutral SECTION kicker and no connective. It still reads.

Narration off strips roles and connectives and leaves the plain document. Click a beat to follow it alone.

PLAN · CARDS — the plan is already an argument

Strategy → surface → contract → risk → proof → order, ending where reality changed the plan. Ten beats, ten map entries.

Two things today's Cards view breaks, fixed here because a beat has to know what it holds: "Affected files" and "Risks and rollback" are markdown TABLES, and src/lib/markdown.ts has no table support (no .md table rule in styles.css either) — they currently land as raw pipe text. "Tasks" flattens its ### Wave headings into generic H3s, losing the wave shape Build runs on.

The counted lines here are all cheap: files with a new-file count, tasks by wave and done, risks with a revert each.

THE WHOLE FEATURE, ON ONE PAGE

Since the labels are fixed, this table IS the implementation — 22 rows and a fallback. No run, no latency, nothing to cache or invalidate, and nothing that can hallucinate a role for a section.

The cost of the choice: the narration is generic where a written sentence would have been specific. The counted line under each title is what buys the specificity back, and it is free.
